beats.narration: Four routes can read the same invoice. A parser costs one unit. A specialist costs four. A frontier model costs nine. A human review costs more. Which route is efficient?
beats.visual_purpose: Make sticker price feel decisive before any acceptance condition appears.
beats.visual_action: One invoice slides onto a sorting table while PARSER, SPECIALIST, FRONTIER, and HUMAN rails grow with fixed fare tokens 1, 4, 9, and MORE; the parser rail lights first.
beats.attention_target: the same invoice facing the four priced rails
beats.object_before: An empty sorting table waits with no route or task object.
beats.object_after: One identified invoice faces four stable candidate routes whose visible prices favor the parser.
beats.composition: Invoice occupies the left third; four parallel rails and fare tokens fill the center and right while the lower caption band stays empty.
beats.motion_curve: The invoice glides in once; rails draw together and fares settle from one to more with increasing visual weight.
beats.visual_inference: Visible price alone makes the parser look efficient before eligibility is tested.
beats.evidence_boundary: The routes and cost units are illustrative, not measured prices.

beats.narration: Price alone cannot answer. The invoice must preserve the total and the vendor. It must also obey the privacy rule. Efficiency begins with an acceptance test, not a model menu.
beats.visual_purpose: Put a fixed predicate and authority condition upstream of route-cost comparison.
beats.visual_action: TOTAL, VENDOR, and PRIVACY seals lift from the invoice and lock into a cyan-and-gold acceptance stencil that spans every route before its fare token.
beats.attention_target: the shared acceptance stencil ahead of all four prices
beats.object_before: Four routes appear comparable only by their fares.
beats.object_after: Every route must pass the same invoice and privacy stencil before its fare can enter comparison.
beats.composition: The stencil forms directly between invoice and rails so eligibility visibly precedes cost.
beats.motion_curve: Three seals copy from the invoice, align without bounce, and close as one keyed aperture.
beats.camera_action: One restrained push-in makes the protected fields legible.
beats.hold_purpose: Allow the viewer to bind all three protected fields to one shared acceptance stencil before route motion resumes.
beats.visual_inference: Only routes preserving the same protected contract are eligible for the cost comparison.
beats.evidence_boundary: The stencil depicts three case fields and does not certify broad correctness or safety.

beats.narration: Send a familiar invoice to the one-unit parser. It extracts every field and passes the test. For this case, the cheap route looks excellent.
beats.visual_purpose: Let the cheap route earn one honest success before showing its failure boundary.
beats.visual_action: A TEMPLATE v3 seal matches the invoice, which travels through the parser and acceptance stencil; all three protected fields illuminate and a green ACCEPTED stamp settles beside the unchanged 1 token.
beats.attention_target: the accepted invoice beside the one-unit fare
beats.object_before: The parser is cheap but has not demonstrated eligibility.
beats.object_after: The familiar invoice passes the depicted contract through the one-unit parser.
beats.composition: The parser rail brightens while other routes stay visible but quiet for comparison.
beats.motion_curve: The invoice moves steadily through version match and three crisp checks before a settled stamp.
beats.camera_action: Track the parser rail at medium scale.
beats.visual_inference: A low-cost route can be adequate for a bounded familiar case.
beats.evidence_boundary: This success is hypothetical and does not establish parser accuracy.

beats.narration: Now damage one digit in the tax line. The parser still returns an answer, but the total is wrong. Repair costs eight units. Review costs three more.
beats.visual_purpose: Attach downstream burden to the cheap route at the moment its output violates the contract.
beats.visual_action: A second invoice enters with one torn TAX digit; the parser still emits an answer, but the TOTAL seal fails and +8 REPAIR and +3 REVIEW bill segments unroll from the parser ticket.
beats.attention_target: the missing tax digit and the attached red/magenta bill segments
beats.object_before: The parser's one-unit success looks reusable and complete.
beats.object_after: The damaged invoice exposes a wrong total and eleven additional units remain attached to the parser route.
beats.composition: The failed invoice remains on the parser rail while its bill unfolds to the right without covering the nine-unit route.
beats.motion_curve: One digit tears away, the failed seal stops sharply, and the bill segments unroll with visible weighted drag.
beats.camera_action: Push closer on the torn field and bill origin.
beats.visual_inference: Repair and review caused by a failed route belong to that route's total bill.
beats.evidence_boundary: The damaged digit and costs are illustrative rather than observed OCR evidence.

beats.narration: The one-unit route has become a twelve-unit route. The verified nine-unit route is now cheaper, even before the downstream error reaches accounting.
beats.visual_purpose: Make the hidden-cost reversal apprehensible as one persistent quantitative state.
beats.visual_action: The 1, +8, and +3 segments latch into one bill reading 1 + 8 + 3 = 12; a balance compares that complete bill with the fixed 9 token and tips toward nine while a downstream-error marker remains open.
beats.object_before: The parser has separate visible and downstream costs but no total comparison.
beats.object_after: The parser route totals twelve and loses the bounded comparison to the nine-unit route.
beats.composition: The equation occupies the center and the balance sits right, with both route identities still visible.
beats.motion_curve: Bill segments click together in sequence; the balance moves once and settles without bounce.
beats.visual_inference: A route's complete caused cost can reverse the ranking implied by its visible fare.
beats.evidence_boundary: The arithmetic is exact only inside the authored invoice example.

beats.narration: That reversal is the Efficient ASI hypothesis in miniature. The efficient route is the least costly authorized route that satisfies the whole contract. It is not the route with the smallest visible meter.
beats.visual_purpose: Generalize from the earned reversal without turning nine into a universal winner.
beats.visual_action: The balance unfolds into three serial stages labeled AUTHORIZED?, CONTRACT PASS?, and COMPLETE COST; the parser's 1 token remains visible outside the final selector until its attached bill joins it.
beats.attention_target: the order of eligibility, contract satisfaction, and complete-cost comparison
beats.object_before: The damaged case shows one reversal but no general route rule.
beats.object_after: Only authorized contract-satisfying routes enter the complete-cost selector.
beats.composition: Three stages align left to right above the retained invoice and bill.
beats.motion_curve: The balance parts translate into gates and ruler while the route tokens preserve identity.
beats.camera_action: Return to the stable wide workshop.
beats.hold_purpose: Keep the three-stage selector and retained route identities visible long enough to separate eligibility from cost.
beats.visual_inference: Minimum cost is conditional on eligibility and the complete declared burden.
beats.evidence_boundary: The selector is a design rule over declared candidates, not a proof of complete or truthful search.

beats.narration: A router can learn this boundary. Familiar templates go to the parser. Uncertain scans escalate to the specialist. High-consequence cases may go directly to a stronger model or a person.
beats.visual_purpose: Show route selection as a conditional policy rather than one globally preferred model.
beats.visual_action: Three invoice variants enter together: TEMPLATE v3 passes to PARSER, an uncertain scan diverts to SPECIALIST, and a high-consequence seal routes past both to FRONTIER/HUMAN; each path retains the same gates.
beats.object_before: The route rule is abstract and could still be mistaken for always-frontier routing.
beats.object_after: Different task conditions select different eligible routes under one contract structure.
beats.composition: The three invoices stack vertically and diverge across the stable route rails without crossing.
beats.motion_curve: Routes reveal one at a time from familiar to uncertain to high consequence, then hold together.
beats.hold_purpose: Let all three condition-dependent route choices coexist before the scene moves to residual accounting.
beats.visual_inference: A route policy can condition on task state while preserving eligibility and fallback boundaries.
beats.evidence_boundary: No learned router or route-quality result is demonstrated.

beats.narration: The failed attempt stays on the bill. Otherwise a routing policy can appear efficient by hiding retries and repairs outside its own measurement window.
beats.visual_purpose: Prevent the route policy from laundering failure through a reset measurement window.
beats.visual_action: The failed parser ticket tries to slide beyond a MEASUREMENT WINDOW bracket; its repair and review segments remain tethered, pull it back, and settle on a RESIDUAL siding owned by the same invoice.
beats.attention_target: the tether preventing the failed bill from leaving the measurement boundary
beats.object_before: The router could count only the successful fallback and forget the cheap failure.
beats.object_after: The failed attempt and its caused burdens remain inside the route's measurement and residual record.
beats.composition: A bracket encloses the route path; the residual siding remains visible below but outside the caption band.
beats.motion_curve: The ticket begins to escape, the tether becomes taut, and the full bill returns in one controlled motion.
beats.camera_action: No camera motion; containment must stay spatially obvious.
beats.visual_inference: Retries and repair remain attributed to the decision that caused them.
beats.evidence_boundary: The tether is an accounting requirement, not proof that real systems discover every delayed cost.

beats.narration: Reuse can compound the gain. Repeated verified work may become a parser or a cached procedure. But the artifact keeps its assumptions. When the invoice format changes, the route expires until it is checked again.
beats.visual_purpose: Show compilation as versioned conditional reuse rather than free permanent capability.
beats.visual_action: Three accepted familiar invoices stamp TEMPLATE v3 into a parser gear with ASSUMPTIONS and TESTS seals; a v4 invoice then fractures the version ring, marks the gear EXPIRED, and diverts to RECHECK.
beats.attention_target: the version ring breaking when v4 arrives
beats.object_before: Repeated accepted work has not yet become durable reuse.
beats.object_after: A versioned artifact serves familiar work but loses eligibility when its assumptions change.
beats.composition: The artifact forms at center from repeated traces; the v4 invoice approaches from left and the recheck siding opens right.
beats.motion_curve: Accepted traces compress into a gear, then the version ring cracks once and the invoice diverts smoothly.
beats.camera_action: One modest push-in on the version ring, then return wide.
beats.hold_purpose: Give the viewer time to track compression into TEMPLATE v3 and the later v4-triggered expiry as separate events.
beats.visual_inference: Verified reuse can reduce repeated work only while versioned assumptions remain current.
beats.evidence_boundary: No lifecycle saving or parser reliability is measured here.

beats.narration: Now change the case. Suppose review becomes nearly free, but privacy risk rises sharply. Would the cheapest compute route still win?
beats.visual_purpose: Test whether the viewer transfers complete-cost reasoning instead of memorizing twelve versus nine.
beats.visual_action: The HUMAN fare token shrinks toward zero while a tall PRIVACY barrier rises across the parser and frontier rails; all route highlights clear and the selector waits.
beats.attention_target: the simultaneous lower review fare and higher privacy barrier
beats.object_before: The damaged case favors the nine-unit route under one fixed contract.
beats.object_after: Two material conditions change in opposite directions and no prior winner remains highlighted.
beats.composition: The shrinking human token and rising privacy barrier occupy opposite sides of the same stable route frame.
beats.motion_curve: Both changes occur together, then every selector motion stops for prediction time.
beats.camera_action: Static matched framing preserves the counterfactual.
beats.visual_inference: Changing noncompute obligations can change route eligibility and total cost.
beats.evidence_boundary: Privacy risk is shown as a constraint, not a precisely measured scalar.

beats.narration: No single answer follows. The complete bill changes the decision because costs caused at one layer surface in another. Model and context spending enter alongside verification and repair. Human review, regression upkeep, and rollback or residual burden finish the same seven-class total.
beats.visual_purpose: Reject a universal route answer and expose the denominator as a structured causal bill.
beats.visual_action: Instead of selecting a route, the prior bill unfolds into the seven modeled classes: MODEL, CONTEXT, VERIFY, REPAIR, HUMAN, REGRESS, and ROLLBACK; each segment feeds the same total line.
beats.attention_target: the seven-class causal bill shared by every route
beats.object_before: The changed case invites another single-price answer.
beats.object_after: Route comparison depends on a vector of eligibility and caused burdens, not compute alone.
beats.composition: The seven bill segments span the upper center while their causal links descend without crossing labels.
beats.motion_curve: The bill unfolds left to right in narration order; route links enter only after all terms are visible.
beats.camera_action: Pull back enough to show the complete bill and all route profiles.
beats.hold_purpose: Keep the seven-class bill visible after construction so model runtime cannot dominate the changed-case comparison.
beats.visual_inference: No route is efficient independently of the complete protected contract and its caused burdens.
beats.evidence_boundary: The seven classes match the local Lean model, but their declared values are trusted inputs rather than measured truth.

beats.narration: A fair experiment would freeze a natural workload and compare several routing policies under matched access. It would count useful accepted work and every material burden created along the way.
beats.visual_purpose: Translate the causal bill into a falsifiable comparison rather than leave it as rhetoric.
beats.visual_action: A FROZEN WORKLOAD crate feeds four policy lanes labeled CHEAPEST, MAXIMAL, ADAPTIVE, and MONOLITH; identical ACCESS seals attach to each while accepted-work counters and causal bills remain separate.
beats.attention_target: the matched access seals and separate accepted-work/burden records
beats.object_before: The complete bill defines what matters but not how to test the hypothesis.
beats.object_after: Four baselines receive the same frozen work and access while useful outcomes and burdens are both counted.
beats.composition: Four equal lanes share one workload source; outcome counters sit above and bills below each lane.
beats.motion_curve: The workload freezes first, access seals duplicate together, then all lanes open simultaneously.
beats.hold_purpose: Allow the four matched policy lanes, outcome counters, and burden records to be compared before the evidence boundary appears.
beats.visual_inference: A credible route comparison must match access and retain both useful outcomes and all material burdens.
beats.evidence_boundary: This is an experimental design requirement; no such comparison result is shown.

beats.narration: Lean proves a narrower result here. Over an authored finite list, the selector returns an eligible route with no greater declared seven-class total than any eligible candidate. It does not prove that the list is complete, the declared costs are true, or any measured efficiency or ASI result.
beats.sync_anchor: Lean proves a narrower result here
beats.visual_purpose: Show the exact formal envelope while keeping candidate completeness, input truth, and measured outcomes outside it.
beats.visual_action: Inside a proof boundary, FINITE LIST, ELIGIBLE MINIMUM, and 7-CLASS TOTAL lock green; COMPLETE SEARCH, COST TRUTH, and MEASURED RESULT remain unfilled sockets outside the proved envelope.
beats.attention_target: the proved finite-selector envelope and its three empty sockets
beats.object_before: The matched experiment and local proof could be mistaken for empirical route optimality.
beats.object_after: The finite selector theorem is visible, while candidate completeness, declaration truth, and measured performance remain open.
beats.composition: The left half contains three proved finite-selector properties; the right half contains three unfilled empirical and completeness sockets.
beats.motion_curve: The proof boundary draws, three finite properties lock in sequence, and the unfilled sockets remain still.
beats.camera_action: No motion; deliberate stillness supports the limitation.
beats.hold_purpose: Let the proved finite envelope and all three unfilled sockets remain visible while the narration separates theorem from measurement.
beats.visual_inference: The local Lean selector proves a bounded minimum over authored eligible candidates and declared seven-class totals.
beats.evidence_boundary: The theorem does not establish complete search, input truth, measured efficiency, transfer, safety, SOTA, AGI, or ASI.

beats.narration: The practical test is simple: a saving is real only if it remains after quality, authority, verification, fallback, and repair have all been paid.
beats.visual_purpose: Close on one reusable test that preserves the episode's full causal structure.
beats.visual_action: The original invoice and its complete bill return; QUALITY, AUTHORITY, VERIFY, FALLBACK, and REPAIR seals stamp in sequence before the remaining green SAVING is weighed under the closing title.
beats.attention_target: the saving that remains only after all five obligations stamp
beats.object_before: The argument boundary states what has not been established.
beats.object_after: One practical complete-cost test remains attached to the invoice and route decision.
beats.composition: The invoice and bill occupy center; five compact seals form a readable arc above the final saving without entering the caption band.
beats.motion_curve: Seals stamp with equal rhythm, the remaining saving settles once, and the final frame holds.
beats.camera_action: Return to the signature comparison frame and hold.
beats.visual_inference: A claimed saving survives only after the obligations and burdens that made the route acceptable are attributed and paid.
beats.evidence_boundary: The closing rule is a measurement contract at argument support, not a measured efficiency result.
